items.title: Lorigerlimab Plus Docetaxel in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tested whether adding lorigerlimab to standard chemotherapy (docetaxel) could delay disease progression in 150 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Participants were randomly assigned 2:1 to receive the combination or docetaxel alone. The study has been completed but results are not yet reported.

items.title: ONC-392 Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial is testing ONC-392 combined with Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose disease progressed after hormone therapy and up to 2 rounds of chemotherapy. The study is active but no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: PSMA-PET Versus Bone Scan for Detecting Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 imaging study compares two types of PET scans (18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET versus 18F-NaF bone scan) to see which better identifies sites of metastatic prostate cancer in the body. The trial is active but no longer enrolling, and aims to improve detection methods for cancer spread.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Care in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares overall survival in men with chemotherapy-naïve metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer receiving xaluritamig plus abiraterone versus investigator's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone). This is a large comparative effectiveness trial currently enrolling patients.

items.title: DS9051b in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human Phase 1 study evaluates the safety, tolerability, and early efficacy signals of DS9051b, a new experimental drug, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and adrenocortical carcinoma. The trial is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: AZD8359 STEAP2-Targeting Antibody in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 study tests AZD8359, a novel antibody drug that targets STEAP2 protein on prostate cancer cells. The trial includes dose escalation and expansion phases to determine the best dose and evaluate effectiveness in men with metastatic prostate cancer. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, can help men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer live longer overall and longer without disease progression compared to standard chemotherapy. This is a large comparative effectiveness trial currently recruiting.

items.title: AAA817 After Lutetium-177 PSMA Failure in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2/3 trial compares AAA817 to standard care in men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose disease progressed after treatment with lutetium-177 PSMA therapy (Pluvicto). This addresses an important clinical need for patients who have exhausted multiple treatment options. Currently recruiting.

items.title: FG-3246 Antibody-Drug Conjugate in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 study evaluates FG-3246, a CD46-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who progressed after one hormone therapy but have not received chemotherapy yet. The trial assesses safety, effectiveness, and how the drug moves through the body. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding mevrometostat to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive (hormone-sensitive) prostate cancer who have not yet received hormone therapy. This targets earlier-stage metastatic disease before castration resistance develops. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 study tests whether combining mevrometostat with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received enzalutamide or abiraterone. This trial aims to improve outcomes before chemotherapy is needed. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Bone Metastases in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial studies the best dose and side effects of combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 (a bone-targeting radioactive treatment) in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to the bones. The combination may enhance treatment effectiveness by blocking DNA repair while delivering targeted radiation. Active but not recruiting.

items.title: Xaluritamig Safety Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety profile of xaluritamig at a proposed treatment regimen in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This early-phase study helps establish the safety foundation for larger trials. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: DCC-2812 GCN2 Activator in Advanced Genitourinary Cancers
items.summary: This Phase 1 multicenter trial evaluates DCC-2812, a novel GCN2 activator, as a single treatment in men with advanced or metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, as well as kidney and bladder cancers. The study tests a new metabolic approach to cancer treatment. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Study of Targetable Proteins in Different Prostate Cancer Types
items.summary: This observational study evaluates the expression of 15 antibody-drug conjugate targets (including PSMA, B7-H3, STEAP1) across different types of prostate cancer, from primary tumors to metastases. Understanding which patients express which targets could guide personalized treatment selection. No longer enrolling but still active.

items.title: Dual BRD4 and AKT Inhibition Overcomes Treatment Resistance
items.summary: Researchers developed a new class of drugs that simultaneously block both BRD4 and AKT proteins in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This dual approach overcomes resistance driven by c-MYC, a common escape mechanism when AKT inhibitors are used alone. Laboratory and preclinical study showing promising results.

items.title: International Analysis of Drug Approvals for Genitourinary Cancers
items.summary: This study analyzed reimbursement rates and clinical benefit of prostate, kidney, and bladder cancer drugs across eight countries (Canada, France, UK nations, Spain, Italy, Portugal) from 2005-2024. The findings show significant variation in which treatments are approved and funded, with Canada and France having the highest approval rates for prostate cancer drugs.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Bone Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model using data from over 3,000 patients to predict overall survival in men with prostate cancer that has spread to the bones who did not have surgery. The model found that Gleason score is more important for prognosis than tumor stage in this population. This could help guide treatment decisions.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic CRPC: Meta-Analysis
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 trials involving 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors combined with other treatments showed better survival benefits than checkpoint inhibitors alone or in dual combinations. The 1-year overall survival was 63% and 2-year was 39% across all patients.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Preserves Bone Health During Enzalutamide Treatment
items.summary: The BonEnza trial studied 89 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer receiving enzalutamide with androgen deprivation therapy. After 18 months, adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening drug) significantly improved bone mineral density at the femoral neck and lumbar spine compared to those not receiving it. This supports bone protection during intensive hormone therapy.
